--- ARTICLE article_id=119988730 published=2025-04-04 ---
HEADLINE: DDA Is Back On Track And Generating Profit: Lieutenant governor
BODY: The lieutenant governor of Delhi is also chairman of Delhi Development Authority (DDA), the agency that controls land in the city. Since May 2022, when VK Saxena took over as LG, DDA has executed several big projects, including beautification of the city during the G20 summit and redevelopment of the Yamuna floodplain besides undertaking reforms which have redefined its role. Saxena spoke to Atul Mathur and Vibha Sharma on a wide range of issues n You will complete three years as LG next month. What have been the major challenges so far? When I came here, there was a strong desire for change in the city so that the national capital truly looked like one. Despite many challenges which prevented us from accomplishing what we wanted, a lot has been achieved. We wished to bring DDA back on track. The biggest challenge was to prevent the misuse of land and curb encroachments. The floodplain needed to be protected and developed. Being the national capital, Delhi should have top-class infrastructure. It should serve as an example for the entire country. However, that did not happen. DDA only built housing complexes. As a result, planned development did not take place. Ideally, in a national capital region, people should work in the city during the day and return to their homes in NCR towns. The reality is the opposite here. Delhi has essentially become a slum city with predominantly lower-income groups living here and working in NCR. A city should be inclusive, serving all sections — lower class, middle class, upper class and elite. Unfortunately, it favours just one section. This needs to be reversed. n What new projects is DDA taking up now? Quite a few. One is a ‘Gold Souk' project. We have floated the expression of interest and the response has been very positive. ‘Gold Souk' does not mean just gold markets — it will include multiple commercial activities. We have also identified land for sports complexes. The current sports infrastructure in Delhi is outdated with some complexes 25-30 years old. We have approved 50 acres of land each for two sports stadiums in Rohini and Narela. We have already issued expressions of interest for them. Some investors have expressed their desire to develop these into world-class facilities. These stadiums will also have hotels and hostels for athletes, similar to international sports hubs. For athletes, there will be facilities for training, lodging, dining and entertainment. We have also started allocating land for corporate offices and invited expressions of interest. When we organised the G20 summit, we realised there were limited options for good hotels. To address this, we have identified locations in Rohini, Narela and Dwarka for new hotels. This marks the beginning of a new development phase for Delhi. n A major problem in Delhi has been that projects are started and then stretch on and on. Will you insist on deadlines being adhered to? We have imposed strict project timelines. The project must be completed within two-and-a-half years of issuing the letter of award and handing over the land. In extremely rare cases, a six-month extension is allowed. I am confident we will succeed because, so far, all our projects have been completed either on time or earlier. Our officials have now adapted to this work culture, ensuring timely completion. n DDA has made changes in its land policy. What is the objective? Earlier, DDA used to auction land. It will now adopt the long-term lease model. Hotels and sports complexes will be leased for 60 years, ensuring that DDA remains owner of the land. It will help make DDA financially self-sufficient. Despite being the owner of a huge number of properties, DDA's annual rental income was shockingly low — just Rs 150 crore. Our goal is to increase this to Rs 1,000 crore. To put things in perspective, NDMC manages a much smaller area but generates Rs 960 crore in rent. We are working to fix this imbalance. n DDA managed to dispose of a large portion of its housing inventory in the last couple of years. How was it achieved? DDA had around 50,000 unsold flats. We are not going for new construction till the existing inventory is disposed of as maintenance alone was costing crores annually. DDA's previous system restricted buyers — if someone already owned a DDA flat, they couldn't apply again. This was unnecessary. If someone wants to buy multiple flats, why stop them? We also abolished the lottery system which forced people to accept random flats even if they disliked the layout or direction. Now, buyers can choose the flat they want. Income restrictions were another issue – we removed limits that prevented high-income buyers from purchasing flats. The buyers will now be able to merge two flats but ensure the strength of the structure is not affected. These changes have had a massive impact. Another reform was in the booking system. Previously, one could book a flat for just Rs 2,000 and hold it for a year. This allowed brokers to manipulate the inventory. We changed this. The buyers now pay 10% upfront, ensuring only serious buyers participate. These reforms have led to record-breaking sales—DDA sold 8,658 flats, generating Rs 3,353 crore in revenue. In total, we have sold flats worth around Rs 4,500 crore. For the first time in DDA's 65-year history, we generated profit. Last year, DDA had a surplus of Rs 535 crore; this year, we expect it to be around Rs 1,300 crore. n DDA recently organised camps in unauthorised colonies under the PM-UDAY scheme. What has been the response? There were very few takers for the PM Uday Scheme and we have revived it through targeted efforts. We have now established a system. People registering the properties under the scheme now get a leather folder which includes an allotment letter, along with all the receipts of payments made. A copy of the MCD-approved site plan and a copy of the certificate received upon completion of construction are included. This had a significant impact. Through these camps, nearly 45,000 people registered their properties. n Will DDA stop constructing housing complexes now? No, no. That won't happen. The DDA inventory currently has about 30,000 EWS units. In the past two years, it has sold around 18,000 houses. Delhi now needs middle-class and high-end flats which we don't have. DDA doesn't need to construct them. Instead, DDA will supervise after handing over the land to societies. n A large number of flats that remained unsold are in a bad shape. How are you ensuring maintenance of the inventory? Maintenance of the inventory happens regularly. If buildings are not maintained, they deteriorate. That's why we prefer selling them, even at lower rates, to avoid liability. Once occupied, RWAs maintain buildings. Vacant properties need attention. Weeds take over and unauthorised people move in. In Narela, we have hired retired army personnel as guards because thefts were happening. n The commercial complexes built by DDA are not in a good condition. What efforts are you making in this direction? You must have seen how we revamped Nehru Place. We built a walkway, improved parking and cleaned up the messy surroundings. Old buildings need to be renovated every 10 years, but I've noticed that several commercial complexes were built 15 years ago and have been locked up since then or encroached upon. It's difficult to evict such people and renovate the complexes. Some small complexes have 12 to 16 shops with restaurant spaces above. Even in Nehru Place, there's a complex that's been closed. We're auctioning it for a hotel project. We identified several such DDA properties, and if we repurpose them properly, Delhi will shine. n Narela has remained neglected. Can it hope for a revival? To accelerate development of the area, we allotted land to five universities, and of them two have even bought flats for their faculty and students. The project didn't move forward as funds were not issued by the state government last year. Without funds, DDA can't sell the land. The newly-elected govt has restarted the process and we expect the construction work to start soon. n Yamuna was divided into 10 sections for undertaking its cleaning. Five or six sections have already been covered, we believe. Yes, some work has been done. The Yamuna riverfront project is also progressing. Each city's riverfront has a different character. People often compare it with the Sabarmati riverfront but the conditions here are different. In Delhi, certain patches can be developed, not the entire stretch. We have developed areas like Asita, Baansera and Vatika, which are green spaces. Riverfront development doesn't always mean concrete structures; natural green zones are also important. There was flooding in the city earlier but our developed areas did not get damaged. That's the key to sustainable riverfront development. We have successfully developed a 10-acre flower field for the first time in the city. The next phase will be grander. Also, I proposed using the river for recreation and transport of goods. I floated the idea with the then CM Arvind Kejriwal but he paid no heed. DDA is now working on a ropeway project on the river too. The cleaning of a section of Najafgarh drain is also being taken up and it too can be used for transporting goods and saving the city from traffic jams. n What is the status of the land pooling policy aimed at planned development in rural areas as well as MPD 2041? We have submitted the draft MPD 2041 to the Centre and they have to take a call. We are expecting the plan to be notified next month. The land pooling policy will follow. n What is your concept of public art? How are you ensuring that public art installed during the G20 summit and later is properly maintained? We have introduced a number of fountains, sculptures and artefacts at roundabouts and public places in the city. People were questioning us prior to the G 20 event about their maintenance but we are doing the task diligently. The agencies concerned, such as PWD, DDA and NDMC, have been asked to maintain them regularly and ensure these don't become defunct. We are even taking up greenery and beautification work beneath flyovers seriously and had a meeting with the CM recently to decide the action plan for implementing the task. n Do you think charging entrance fees for neighbourhood parks is a good idea? Will this be extended to other places? We are not imposing entrance fees at all parks. These are selected sites which are usually bigger in size and where DDA has made a lot of investment to provide facilities. You won't believe that 1100 tickets are sold in a day at a park in Noida where a nominal fee is charged to ensure these areas are maintained properly and remain secure for visitors. n Now that the govt has changed, what will be your role? My role as Delhi's guardian will continue. I have been a local guardian earlier and will remain so.
--- END ARTICLE ---

HEADLINE: Delhi: Milkman found dead on Heliport road in Rohini
BODY: NEW DELHI: The body of a 35-year-old milkman was found on Heliport road in Rohini area in the national capital, said the Delhi police officials on Monday. The police have registered an FIR. The deceased has been identified as Pradeep who hails from Rithala. The police informed that the information of the presence of a "corpse" was received early in the morning after which the station house officer of the Begumpur police station was rushed to the spot. The milkman along with his motorcycle was found at the spot of the incident. Further investigation into the matter is underway.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=81741137 published=2021-03-28 ---
HEADLINE: Gangster who fled from hospital shot dead in Delhi
BODY: NEW DELHI: Within sixty hours of escaping from police custody amid a shootout at GTB Hospital, notorious gangster Kuldeep Maan alias Fajja was killed in another dramatic encounter with cops inside a flat at a housing society in Delhi’s Rohini early Sunday. The special cell got a tipoff on Fajja’s hideout at 9pm Saturday. A crack team of 24 cops, backed by a SWAT squad, reached the society at 1.20am, secured the residents and rang the bell of the flat. The door was opened, police barged in and Fajja started firing. Two cops were hit, but saved by their bulletproof vests. Fajja soon went down and was declared dead in hospital. Fajja opened fire as cops rushed in after ringing the bell thrice Just after escaping from police custody at Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital, Fajja went to a contact, Bhupender Bhuttan, in outer Delhi, collected money and headed towards Rohini according to the directions given to him. Fajja was holed up with his aide Yogender Dahiya for two days at a flat in Tulsi Apartment in Rohini’s Sector 14 and tracking news on his escape, but didn’t use phones or internet, deputy commissioner of police (Special Cell) Pramod Kushwaha claimed. All this while, a team of officers led by ACP Lalit Mohan Negi and Hriday Bhushan from the New Delhi Range of the Special Cell started tracking Fajja and his associates. The cops received a tipoff about Bhuttan and detained him on Saturday evening. It was he who gave police the location of Fajja’s hideout around 9pm. While a surveillance team furtively kept watch at the housing society and the flat since 10pm, the main assault team comprising the two ACPs and inspectors Sunil Rajain and Ravinder Joshi along with 20 others reached the apartment at around 1.20am. The guards at the gate were asked to co-operate and adjacent residents were secured after the presence of “two suspicious men” was confirmed in the flat located on the ground floor. The cops rang the bell thrice — a pre-decided code — of the flat. Once the cops rushed in, Fajja started firing at them from his pistol after taking cover. The cops shot back, and he soon fell on the floor after getting hit. He was taken to Ambedkar hospital and was declared dead on arrival. His postmortem was conducted at the AIIMS and the body handed over to his family on Sunday afternoon. The walls of the flat were riddled with bullets: Fajja fired eight rounds and the cops replied with 12. Dahiya didn’t fire at police and surrendered unhurt the moment the policemen barged in. A pistol was found on him. On March 25, amidst the shootout on the premises of Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital, Delhi Armed Police personnel had shot dead a criminal and injured another after they tried to free Fajja from their custody on Thursday noon. Fajja had been brought to the GTB Hospital for a checkup. Soon after the incident, police officers sealed all border points and alerted patrol to keep watch on suspicious elements. Dozens of raids were conducted at possible hideouts, and criminals outside and inside jails were interrogated for clues. Finally, the breakthrough came on Saturday night. “Fajja was previously involved in 11 criminal cases, including five brutal murders and three cases of armed robberies, extortion and other cases,” DCP Kushwaha said.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=107610684 published=2024-02-12 ---
HEADLINE: Inside criminal minds: How these tools are helping Delhi police nail lies
BODY: NEW DELHI: Crimes and criminals in Delhi are prompting investigators to rely increasingly on psychiatric assessment of suspects, something rarely done in the past. Whether it be Shraddha Walkar's murder in south Delhi, Swiss national Nina Berger's killing in west Delhi or even the Parliament security breach cases, police have sought the assistance of forensic psychologists to read the suspects' minds. The trend indicates a changing pattern of people accused of heinous crimes being seemingly normal individuals, requiring the psychology division of Forensic Science Laboratory, Rohini, to assist the cops last year in 130 cases, an increase of about 27% from the previous year. Forensic officials from the Delhi division that TOI spoke to said there were now six units, each headed by a senior psychologist, to cope with the rising number of cases requiring their expertise. "Forensic psychological analysis aims to assist investigators in identifying potentially deceptive individuals and exonerating innocent people," explained a senior official. Many break down during interrogation and confess to their crimes, but there are hardened ones who continually frustrate the law enforcers. They are the ones on whom psychological tests are carried out. In the Shraddha Walkar case, the psychologists wanted to determine why Aaftab Poonawala dismembered her body and dumped them in different locations. They wanted to ascertain what caused so much hatred in his mind to undertake such a gruesome task. Psychological analysis was also important because Aaftab was constantly taking police on wild goose chases using his innate abilities. In the Parliament breach case, the cops wanted to know the mindset that planned and implemented the intrusion into the Lok Sabha. Gurpreet Singh, the alleged killer of Berger, was subjected to tests and the analysis reported signs of "disturbed behaviour". Deepa Verma, director, FSL, said that the primary role of a forensic psychologist begins with understanding and evaluating the mental and emotional state of individuals suspected of committing crimes. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, division head (crime scene), FSL, said, "The psychologist keeps a close tab on the accused individual's body language and behavioural patterns during test sessions. The focus is on gathering details hidden within their subconscious mind." Another official explained that while suspects might answer some questions without significant physical reactions, some expert-led questions could trigger involuntary responses, such as pupil dilation or uneven leg movement. If the initial tests don't yield the expected results, police can seek court permission for more extensive investigative measures, such as narco-analysis or polygraph tests. In any case, court permission and the suspect's consent are mandatory for any of these procedures. During the narco test, a doctor administers a drug to the suspect in an operation theatre to induce a hypnotic state. Before the tests, the individual is subjected to a series of medical tests to assess his or her health condition. During the hypnotic state, the experts asks questions while recording the entire process. In a polygraph test, instruments such as electrodes and cardio-cuffs are attached to measure heartbeat breathing pattern, etc., when the suspect is made to answer questions related to the crime. In many cases, experts use a layered voice stress analyser to dissect psychological reactions like emotions, stress, uneasiness, energy levels and voice concentration. FSL also has brain fingerprinting instruments that use electro-encephalography (EEG) to map brainwave patterns. This helps investigators determine whether the suspects have knowledge about the crime. There were cases where FSL experts had also handled psychological autopsies. "In an effort to understand the mind of a deceased, a psychological autopsy delves into medical records, interviews friends and family, and gathers information about their mental state before death," the officer explained.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=123857760 published=2025-09-12 ---
HEADLINE: Drug bust: Delhi Police arrests three, including Nigerian national
BODY: New Delhi: Delhi Police's crime branch has arrested three people, including a Nigerian national, in connection with an international drug syndicate and seized 194 grams of cocaine worth Rs 2.25 crore from them. According to police, a tip-off was received on Sept 6 that two men—Rahul Wadhwa (32) and Abdul Kadir (29)—would be delivering a cocaine consignment in sector-36, Rohini. Acting on the information, a team apprehended the duo around 3pm while they were allegedly conducting a drug deal. Police recovered 85 grams of cocaine from their possession, and a case was registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. "The men told police that the cocaine was supplied by a Nigerian national, Chimezie Lazarus Ndedinigwe, alias Zudo (35), a resident of Mehrauli, who controls the cocaine distribution in Delhi-NCR," said DCP (crime) Pankaj Kumar. Based on the lead, the team tracked down Zudo to his residence in Mehrauli on Sept 10 and arrested him. An additional 109 grams of cocaine was seized from him. Investigations revealed that Kadir, a former taxi driver, was lured into drug trafficking by Zudo, who paid him Rs 1,000 per delivery. Kadir later introduced Wadhwa into the network. Police said Zudo came to India in Jan 2023 for medical treatment but took to selling cocaine in Delhi, Gurgaon, Meerut, Chandigarh and Haldwani.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=126601515 published=2026-01-17 ---
HEADLINE: Punjabi singer Dilnoor receives threat call demanding Rs 10 crore for Bollywood singer B Praak; caller linked to Bishnoi gang
BODY: NEW DELHI: In a chilling escalation of extortion attempts targeting the Punjabi music industry, renowned Bollywood and Punjabi singer B Praak received a death threat, allegedly from the Lawrence Bishnoi syndicate. The threat was delivered via his associate singer, Dilnoor. The incident took place on January 5, when Dilnoor received 2 missed calls from an international number. When the calls persisted on the afternoon of January 6, Dilnoor briefly answered but disconnected after sensing something suspicious. Shortly after, a voice recording was sent to him from a person identifying himself as Anmol Bishnoi (referred to as Arzoo Bishnoi in initial reports), the brother of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi, who is believed to be operating from abroad. The audio message issued a direct ultimatum: pay 10 crore within 1 week or face dire consequences. In the recording, the caller explicitly told Dilnoor to convey the message to B Praak, stating, "Tell B Praak we want 10 crore. You have 1 week. No matter which country you go to, if we find anyone associated with you, we will cause harm. Do not take this as a fake call. If he cooperates, it’s fine; otherwise, tell him we will bury him in the dirt. " Following receipt of this threat, Dilnoor submitted a written complaint to the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) in Mohali on January 6. Cops initiated an investigation into the matter, though the high-profile nature of the target heightened security concerns within the entertainment circuit. This threat follows a pattern of recent violence attributed to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Since the start of the New Year, the gang was linked to several incidents in Delhi, including a case in Rohini where 25 rounds were fired outside a businessman’s house, and similar attacks in West Vihar and East Delhi. The gang’s modus operandi typically involves an initial phone threat followed by gunfire at the victim's residence to instil fear. While Delhi Police recently arrested several suspects involved in previous shootings following encounters, the threat to B Praak highlights the persistent reach of extortionists targeting celebrities.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=96995305 published=2023-01-14 ---
HEADLINE: Gogi gang member demands Rs 20 lakh extortion from Rohini businessman, held
BODY: NEW DELHI: The crime branch of Delhi Police recently arrested a Gogi gang member for allegedly demanding an extortion of Rs 20 lakh from a Rohini-based car dealer. The accused was identified as Sumit alias Fimmi. One semi-automatic pistol and four live rounds were recovered from his possession. He was previously involved in three cases of attempted murder. Special commissioner of police (crime) Ravindra Singh Yadav said on receiving information about the movements of the accused, a team under the supervision of Vichitra Veer Singh was constituted, which arrested Fimmi in Nangli Vihar Extension. Police said Fimmi and his accomplice, Hemant, opened fire upon one Nishant, a resident of Bawana, in 2017. In the same year, he opened fire on one Sumit too. He was absconding and was declared a proclaimed offender in these cases. In 2018, he, along with his associate, Sanam Dagar, allegedly opened fire on one Monu Bajitpuria, and was arrested by the Bawana police. He was released on bail in 2020 and last year, in December, to arrange money for his gang, he and his associates made an extortion call to a Rohini-based car dealer and demanded Rs 20 lakh from him. Fimmi’s brother, Hitesh, is a sharpshooter and is presently lodged in Mandoli Jail.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=87378714 published=2021-10-29 ---
HEADLINE: Delhi Police gun down shooter of Gogi gang in Rohini
BODY: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Friday shot dead an alleged shooter of Gogi gang following a brief exchange of fire in Rohini early on Friday. The cops said that the man was wanted in a murder case and a parole jumper. The man has been identified as 25-year-old Deepak Sharma, a resident of Jind in Haryana. He allegedly opened fire and injured two policemen, while a third was hit on his bulletproof vest. He was shot in retaliatory fire, senior police officers said. Police received input on Friday regarding a gangster wanted for a murder in Sector-16, Rohini, who was also a parole jumper in two cases of Begumpur and Rohtak. “A team from Begumpur police station laid a trap where Sharma was supposed to come. Sharma arrived on a white motorcycle around 5.15am and identified. He was asked to surrender, but he opened fire. The bullet hit inspector Arvind Kumar’s bulletproof jacket. Constables Vikas and Sunny were also hit,” said a police officer. “Police fired back in self defence and a bullet hit Sharma.” An ambulance was called to take two policemen and Sharma to a hospital, where he was declared brought dead. “Forensics team recovered his gun from the scene of crime,” said the officer. Police have registered a case of attempt to murder to further probe the matter.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=86494441 published=2021-09-24 ---
HEADLINE: CJI N V Ramana expresses serious concern over shootout in Delhi
BODY: NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India N V Ramana on Friday expressed serious concern over the firing incident at Rohini Court complex in Delhi in which two assailants in lawyers attire gunned down gangster Jindra Gogi, who was in judicial custody. CJI Ramana wanted to visit the scene of the incident and take stock of the security arrangements inside the court complex but was advised against visiting the crime scene. The CJI, however, conveyed his deep distress over the incident to Delhi high court Chief Justice D N Patel and asked him to take all necessary measures, in consultation with the Union government, for arranging foolproof security arrangements in all court complexes within the national capital territory. CJI told the Delhi CJ that this is not the first firing incident inside the Delhi court complexes and desired that the Delhi police and other authorities should be taking adequate measures and installing equipment at appropriate places inside the court complexes to ensure that the courts functioned without any violent incident. The CJI was told by the Delhi HC CJ D N Patel that he is in touch with the Delhi police on the incident. The Delhi police informed the Delhi HC CJ that one of the major security threat to the court complexes arises because of the apparent reluctance and refusal of lawyers to get frisked physically by the police personnel deployed at the entry points of court complexes. The CJI was informed that during the firing by assailants that killed Gogi and the retaliatory firing by the Delhi Police personnel, in which the two assailants were neutralised, a stray bullet had hit the dais of the judicial officer at the nearby courtroom but luckily without hurting anyone. The CJI said judicial officers, judges and lawyers as well as litigants must feel secure inside the court complexes to enable smooth dispensation of justice. The SC had taken suo motu cognisance of the inadequate security cover provided to the judges and court complexes after the murder of Dhanbad judge in July. It had asked the state government to give details of the security inside court complexes as well as to judges at their residences. On August 17, the SC had read the riot act to major states for disregarding deadline to file affidavits detailing security measures for judges and court complexes and imposed Rs 1 lakh cost on each. The Rohini incident will force the CJI to expedite the hearing on the issue of judges and lawyers' security. It is expected that the suo motu matter would be listed next week.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=85770347 published=2021-08-30 ---
HEADLINE: 12 held, fake call centre busted in Delhi's Rohini
BODY: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police 's cyber cell has busted a fake call centre and arrested 12 people for allegedly duping innocent persons in the name of offering personal loans at low-interest rates under a government scheme. A computer, 29 mobile phones, one tablet, internet routers, order book receipts and incriminating data in mobiles has also been recovered, the police said. According to the police, the accused allegedly cheated people from across India under the false pretext of offering personal loans at low-interest rates under the scheme. The accused have been sent to judicial custody and further investigation is underway.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=84303161 published=2021-07-10 ---
HEADLINE: Cops fire at 5 criminals in 24 hours, 9 shootouts in 4 days
BODY: New Delhi: In a period of 24 hours since Friday, Delhi Police’s Special Cell opened fire on five miscreants during a drive to curb crime. A snatcher of outer Delhi faced Special Cell’s ire on Friday and then later that day, a history-sheeter of Narela and his associate were shot. On Saturday morning, two gunrunners from Meerut were shot at. In fact, nine shootouts were reported in the last four days. All operations were conducted by teams led by Sanjeev Yadav, DCP (Special Cell). According to the DCP, snatcher identified as Javed alias Pager was arrested after a shootout in Shahbad Dairy area early on Friday. Javed is involved in more than 17 cases. Later, around 9pm on Friday, two snatchers, named Yashpal alias Bhola and Bicky alias Vikas, were intercepted in Rohini. They were ordered to surrender, but they fired at cops leading to a shootout. The two were injured and taken to hospital. Yashpal is previously involved in more than 15 cases of robberies and snatching in Mangolpuri. Then, in the early hours of Saturday, the cops received information about two illegal firearms suppliers, Abdul Wahab and Farman, both residents of Meerut. When police tried to stop them in Dwarka, a shootout ensued. Five sophisticated pistols and 60 live cartridges were recovered. The two had to be hospitalised with injuries. Prior to these operations, Special Cell was able to arrest five hardened criminals after an exchange of fire. In an operation in the intervening night of Tuesday and Wednesday, the cops arrested Sazee and Tajim Saifi after a shootout near the Karni Singh shooting range in south Delhi’s Prahladpur. On Thursday around 6pm, personnel of the Special Cell’s northern range cornered notorious criminal Satish in Rohini. Involved in over 25 cases of robbery, burglary and snatchings, Satish was recently booked under MCOCA. He fired at the cops but was overpowered. A criminal named Deepak was arrested after a shootout near sector 36 in Rohini, while a notorious snatcher, Pradeep Gurri, was also arrested. DCP Yadav has formed teams under ACPs Sanjay Dutt and Jasbir Singh to fight street criminals. Yadav said, “Delhi Police is on its toes keeping an eye on bikers at key points, including crime hotspots, and Special Cell has specifically been tasked to tackle gun-wielding criminals committing street crimes.” In many recent cases, the criminals, when facing resistance, had opened fire on innocent victims because of which Special Cell was asked to retaliate ‘proportionately’, a police officer revealed.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=114156694 published=2024-10-11 ---
HEADLINE: 28-year-old stabbed to death in Delhi's Vijay Vihar for friendship with girl
BODY: NEW DELHI: A 28-year-old food delivery agent was stabbed six times by four men in Vijay Vihar on Thursday, causing his death. Police said the murder was a fallout of a dispute over a woman friend. The deceased was identified as Deepak . He lived with his family in Vijay Vihar, Rohini. Police got a PCR call at 5.20 pm on Wednesday that alerted the force about a stabbing near Nirankari Bhawan in Rohini. A police team that went to the spot found a man lying in a pool of blood. People had gathered from nearby. He was taken to the hospital, where he was declared dead. A case of murder was registered. During the investigation, police found out that four people were involved in the crime. "On the day of the incident, Deepak was riding his motorcycle in a lane adjacent to his house when he was waylaid by the men, who stabbed him half a dozen times and fled," an officer said. Further investigation revealed that Deepak had a past criminal history. There were three cases against him. "After scanning CCTV footage, we apprehended 19-year-old Nikhil Tomar, who had committed multiple offences as a juvenile. He was nabbed from Vijay Vihar and the knife used in the crime was recovered from Prem Nagar. Raids are being conducted to nab the other three accused," a police source said.
--- END ARTICLE ---

HEADLINE: Delhi: Fake call centre busted, 24 held for duping people by offering mobile phones at cheap rates
BODY: NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has busted a fake call centre and arrested 24 people, including 15 women, from Rohini area, officials said on Saturday. The accused duped victims, mainly from the northeastern states and Odisha, on the pretext of offering them mobile phones at cheap rates through a lottery scheme, they said. Police said Ramkumar (34), Shyam Kumar (35) and Govind (22), all residents of Sultanpuri here, together owned the call centre. On Friday, the police received information about the fake call centre operating at Rohini Sector-7 which allegedly duped people on the pretext of offering them mobiles at cheap rates through a lottery scheme, a senior police officer said. "The police raided the call centre and nabbed the accused. Enquiry revealed that most of the victims belonged to the northeastern states," deputy commissioner of police (Rohini) Pranav Tayal said. During interrogation, it was revealed that the accused used to collect mobile number of people residing in other states from the internet, the DCP said. They randomly made calls to people across the country and induced them with lucrative offers. They told the people that their number had been selected for the offer in which they will get a mobile phone worth Rs 17,000 on payment of just Rs 4,500, police said. In order to gain the confidence of customers, they used the post office as logistics service provider. However, instead of sending mobiles, they would send cheap wallets, belt, soaps etc. in the parcel, police said. Police also raided the warehouse of the accused situated at Rohini Sector-20 and recovered packets that were ready to be delivered. The three owners of fake call centre were also nabbed from there, police said. Police recovered three computers, 52 mobiles, 384 packets and other items.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=91276970 published=2022-05-03 ---
HEADLINE: Delhi: Gang that used fake website to dupe job aspirants busted
BODY: NEW DELHI: Three graduates, including a woman, have been arrested for allegedly duping people on the pretext of getting them jobs in reputed foreign companies through a fake website . The accused have been identified as Sonam Kumari (25), Rahul Kumar (22) and Rajat Kumar (23), all from UP. Seven mobile phones, a laptop, eight ATM cards and 12 SIM cards have been seized from them. Deputy commissioner of police (Rohini) Pranav Tayal said that investigation was taken up following a complaint in a cheating case. On the basis of money trail, it was learnt that the cheated amount had been transferred in various bank accounts. "On the basis of deep analysis, some suspects were zeroed in. Subsequently, technical surveillance was mounted on the suspects and it was learnt that the alleged were operating from the area of Ashutosh Colony in Bareilly, UP. Accordingly, a raid was conducted in Bareilly and the suspects were apprehended," the DCP said.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=84643763 published=2021-07-22 ---
HEADLINE: Prison authorities allow Sushil Kumar to watch TV ahead of Tokyo Olympics
BODY: NEW DELHI: Delhi Prison authorities on Thursday allowed two-time Olympic medallist Sushil Kumar , lodged in Tihar jail in connection with the Chhatrasal Stadium brawl , to watch television in the common area of his ward ahead of the Olympic games, which is set to begin on July 23, officials said. On July 2, Kumar through his advocate had urged prison authorities to provide him a television to remain updated about wrestling matches and other happenings outside the jail. The Covid-hit Olympic games will begin at Tokyo in Japan on July 23. Director General ( Delhi Prisons ) Sandeep Goel said, "We have allowed Sushil Kumar to watch television in the common area of his ward along with others since the Olympics is set to begin from tomorrow. "He has made a request through his lawyer for a TV to stay updated about wrestling matches and other happenings." Kumar was arrested along with co-accused Ajay Kumar on May 23 from outer Delhi's Mundka area. He and his associates allegedly assaulted wrestler Sagar Dhankar and two of his friends Sonu and Amit Kumar on the intervening night of May 4 and 5 over a property dispute. Dhankar, 23, succumbed to injuries later. Kumar, who is facing charges of murder, culpable homicide and kidnapping, was shifted to Tihar jail number 2 from Mandoli jail where he was lodged earlier. Police said 12 accused, including Kumar , have so far been arrested in connection with the Chhatrasal Stadium brawl case. The police have claimed that Kumar is the "main culprit and mastermind" of the murder and said there is electronic evidence in which he and his associates could be seen beating Dhankar. Last month, a Delhi court had dismissed an application filed by Kumar, seeking special food and supplements in the prison, saying that they are not the "essential need or necessity". Kumar had moved the Rohini court seeking special food, supplements and exercise bands in the prison, asserting that these are extremely necessary for him to maintain his health and performance.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=95107053 published=2022-10-26 ---
HEADLINE: Delhi: Kin allege murder, polygraph tests match friends’ claim youth fell off terrace & died
BODY: NEW DELHI: Over three months after a 25-year-old man was found dead in Rohini in mysterious circumstances, the polygraph tests conducted on his four friends have suggested that Rohit indeed did fall the three-storey building on the night of July 17, said police. In August, police filed a case of culpable homicide on his family’s complaint and questioned the four friends with whom he was last seen. According to their statements, a party was going on the terrace of a friend’s house when Rohit allegedly fell and died. “The polygraph test results have corroborated their initial claims before police,” said an official. However, the probe is continuing as the results of polygraph tests are not admissible as evidence in court; they only aide in the investigation. In August, TOI reported about the police plan to conduct the tests. According to preliminary investigations, Rohit was found lying with his face down on the adjacent building premises the following day. Police took him to hospital, where he was declared dead. His family was informed on July 19 after the body was identified. Rohit’s sister, Kavita, alleged that there was ample evidence to prove that he was murdered. “I myself went to the spot to see what circumstances could have led to his death. There were so many injuries on his body; there was no way that he could have fallen on his own. We have filed a petition in the high court and the next date of hearing is February 7, 2023. We don’t trust these polygraph tests, they don’t mean anything to us. Our family will fight the case and seek justice for my brother,” said Kavita, one of the three sisters. Rohit was their only brother, said Kavita. The accused had told police that they had got scared and ran away. Police then decided to conduct the polygraph tests.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=91994108 published=2022-06-03 ---
HEADLINE: Another Delhi-based doctor arrested in kidney racket
BODY: NEW DELHI: While probing the kidney racket case busted on Monday, Delhi Police arrested another doctor on Friday from northwest Delhi. He was working at a private hospital in Uttam Nagar. Police identified the suspect as Dr Priyansh, 34, alias Sameer, a resident of Rohini . He completed his medical studies in Uttar Pradesh, earning his MBBS degree from a college in Bareilly and the MS degree from a college in Etawah. Benita Mary Jaiker, DCP (South), said the arrested man was a surgeon. During investigation, the cops found that Sameer was assisting the main accused, Kuldeep Ray, in the transplantation racket and he was paid Rs 1 lakh per transplant. "Though a surgeon, Sameer assisted Kuldeep, an OT technician, in the transplant surgery. He used to suture the cuts after surgery," an investigator said. Cops suspect that Sameer might be part of the Rajasthan gang for which Ray worked earlier. “The Rajasthan gang used to pay Ray Rs 50,000-1 lakh for surgery while other specialist surgeons got a lot more money. Ray took a much longer time during the procedure than other doctors. This and the money led to the dispute,” the investigator disclosed. The gang only summoned Ray when the recipient had to pay Rs 10-20 lakh for the transplantation. “In cases where the recipient was paying Rs 50-80 lakh, the gang used to call other surgeons.” The cops discovered that before any transplantation, the accused met at different places, including prominent hotels, to discuss the illegal transplant surgery. Sources said that Ray also met a few doctors at hotels to lure them to join his gang. "All this information is being verified," the investigating officer said. Sources said it is being suspected that Ray also carried out the transplants in other states apart from Rajasthan and Delhi. An officer said that Ray was always not able to make a proper incision on the donor's stomach as would be done by expert surgeons. “He was not properly aware of the kidney location and thus made such cuts,” the officer explained. Ray’s group was planning to shift from their clinic in Gohana, Haryana, but police swooped on them before they could do that. “The Gohana residents were becoming suspicious about the activities at the clinic so Ray and his team were planning to change their location,” the officer said. The officer also revealed that the gang had a pan-India connection. “There is a possibility that Ray had formed other gangs in different states. We are looking into this aspect also,” the officer said. Meanwhile, police are likely to seek the help of medical experts in this illegal organ trade case.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=108651858 published=2024-03-20 ---
HEADLINE: Delhi health minister urges LG to take strict against assistant professor in sexual harassment case
BODY: NEW DELHI: Delhi's Health Minister, Saurabh Bharadwaj , on Wednesday wrote to Lieutenant Governor (L-G) VK Saxena, urging him to take strict action against Assistant Professor accused of sexually assaulting MBBS students at BSA college, Rohini. Minister Saurabh Bharadwaj emphasised the safety and security of the female students in the medical college, questioning why the Secretary (Health) didn't report a sexual harassment incident, and why the Chief Secretary (CS) is defending him. On Monday, the Health Minister directed the CS to take strict action against the Professor accused of sexually assaulting MBBS students at BSA College, Rohini. Bharadwaj had also directed immediate action against the Principal and Head of Department (HoD) for their reprehensible act of pressuring students to withdraw their complaint. However, on Wednesday, the Minister expressed his disappointment for inaction in the matter saying, 'shocked to see the CS is trying to defend the culprits by lame excuses.' "CS is justifying the Health Secretary for not disclosing this incident of sexual assault to the Minister, despite clear instructions by the Health Minister to the Secretary (Health) to report such incidents promptly," said Bhardawaj. "Victims had to finally approach police in an individual capacity when the Vigilance Department and Health Department failed to take timely action. The Internal Complaints Committee was dragging the matter and did not submit its report in 1.5 months," Bharadwaj said in his letter to LG. The Minister's letter condemns the CS for defending the Health Secretary, Vigilance, and ICC in his ATR. On Tuesday, days after female MBBS students from Delhi's Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College accused an Assistant Professor of Pharmacology, Salim Sheikh , of sexual harassment during a viva examination, the Directorate of Vigilance urged the Health & Family Welfare Department to propose disciplinary action against the accused. Taking cognisance of media reports, the Vigilance Department highlighted the need for action in a letter addressed to the Secretary of the Health & Family Welfare Department. According to the FIR registered on February 22, an MBBS student from the 2021 batch alleged that on January 31, during a practical examination in the pharmacology department, she was subjected to inappropriate and irrelevant questions by the Assistant Professor during her viva. The questions made her feel 'uncomfortable'. In her complaint, the student described how Sheikh positioned her chair unusually close to him, deviating from the usual setup where students sit across from the teacher.
--- END ARTICLE ---

--- ARTICLE article_id=130965462 published=2026-05-08 ---
HEADLINE: Crime to conviction in only 18 days for this robbery accused
BODY: New Delhi: Delhi Police has secured the conviction of a man accused of assaulting and robbing a woman within 18 days of the crime, with the chargesheet being filed in just five days and the trial court conducting day-to-day proceedings. On the evening of April 18, when a 21-year-old woman was waiting near Prahladpur bus stand in the Shahbad Dairy area of northwest Delhi, a man had approached and physically assaulted her before forcibly snatching her iPhone 15 and fleeing the spot. Hearing the victim’s cries for help, head constable Vikram, who was patrolling nearby, rushed to the spot and began chasing the accused along with the victim. The accused, identified as 22-year-old Pankaj, a resident of a JJ colony in Bawana, was apprehended within minutes near a colony’s gate. The robbed phone was found on him and seized. Based on the complainant's statement, police registered a case under sections 309 (robbery) and 317 (stolen property) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at the Shahbad Dairy police station. The probe was completed within 72 hours and the chargesheet was filed before the Rohini court within five days of the incident on April 23. “The chargesheet was filed in record time,” claimed DCP (outer north) Hareshwar V Swami. The trial court of judicial magistrate first class Bharti Beniwal then took cognisance of the chargesheet and started proceedings on a day-to-day basis. The charges against the accused, who remained in custody throughout the trial proceedings, were framed on April 29, barely 11 days after the robbery. On May 6, the court completed the proceedings and convicted Pankaj. Violent robbery and street crime cases generally continue to languish in courts for months, and often years — one of the key reasons why many victims eventually lose hope and stop pursuing them. The current case has emerged as one of the fastest convictions secured in a street robbery matter under the new criminal laws, police claimed. According to police, the case was part of a special drive launched by the outer north district to fast-track street crime prosecutions in line with directions issued by Delhi Police commissioner Satish Golchha. "Eight street crime cases from different police stations in the district were shortlisted for expedited investigation and trial under the initiative,” the DCP said. The court, while convicting the accused, also appreciated the prompt recovery of the stolen property and the manner in which evidence was collected during the investigation. The police team involved in the case is likely to be rewarded for the speedy investigation and prosecution.
--- END ARTICLE ---
